family/F_gru8.title: GRU 8×2
family/F_gru8.purpose: Compare saved network configurations on the same family-study data and targets. Architecture-specific dropout settings differ; this is not a perfectly isolated cell-type change.
family/F_gru8.target: Each saved run’s own training target. Compare within this family study; not a direct ranking against the controlled experiments.
family/F_gru8.protocol: Fast: batch 64, up to 150 epochs, patience 15; 0.2 s history; source session 1 → retest session 2.

main/session-passive.title: 0.5 s window + retest passive map
main/session-passive.purpose: Predict voluntary ankle torque from the last 0.5 s of muscle activity, scored against a target whose passive part is re-measured in the test session.
main/session-passive.target: Active torque = measured torque − passive torque at that angle. Session 1 (training) uses its own passive map; session 2 (test) uses a passive map measured again in session 2.
main/session-passive.protocol: Train on session 1, test on session 2. 50 samples at 100 Hz (0.5 s) of four muscle envelopes plus angle; LSTM 8×2, dropout 0.3; up to 60 epochs, patience 12, batch 64; seeds 0–9.

notes: YES: trials 27, 29, 31 and 33 are the retest pushes at p1–p4. Their notes in the recording wrongly say “passive”; their angles and torque match the session-1 pushes. Session-1 passive values come from the lab worksheet.
IES: the recording has no passive trials. The passive table in the IES metadata document (measured before session 1) is used for both sessions.
JM: the still-hold rule already ignores the movement in passive trial 21, so its passive map needs no fix.
CH: added to the subject list; nothing else changed.

norm/N0.title: N0 · session-1 maximum (control)
norm/N0.target: Total measured torque, nothing subtracted. The passive table plays no part in training or scoring.

settings: Session 1 → session 2 · 8 angles · one ~90 s trial per angle
4 EMG envelopes (GM, GL, SOL, TA) + ankle angle, 100 Hz
0.2 s = 20 samples → torque at the window’s last sample
Yes: each position’s target ÷ its standard deviation
steps: EMG: band-pass 30–300 Hz, rectify, 2 Hz low-pass → envelope (1 kHz), then down-sampled to 100 Hz.
Scale: Each muscle envelope is divided by the largest value it reached anywhere in session 1 (one sample of the 1 kHz envelope). Session 2 is divided by the same four numbers.
Standardise the 5 inputs (mean 0, sd 1) with session 1’s training statistics.
Cut 0.2 s windows sliding by one sample. Each session-1 trial: first 80 % to fit, last 20 % to stop training.
Train the LSTM on the target ÷ each position’s standard deviation, then multiply its predictions back (Nadam, lr 0.003, batch 8, ≤ 200 epochs, early stopping after 25).
Predict every window of session 2, which the model never saw.
Score each position on every 100 Hz sample: R² = 1 − Σ(y − ŷ)² / Σ(y − ȳ)², MAE = mean |y − ŷ|. Median over seeds, then median across positions; R² below 0 is shown as 0.

norm/N0.purpose: Each muscle is divided by the largest value it reached anywhere in session 1: one single sample of the 1 kHz envelope. Session 2 is divided by the same numbers. This is the control: the same scaling as the baseline.
norm/N0.protocol: Train on session 1, test on session 2. Total torque, 0.2 s window (20 samples at 100 Hz) of four muscle envelopes plus angle. Balanced positions (each position’s target ÷ its standard deviation). LSTM 8×2, dropout 0.3, batch 8, at most 200 epochs, early stopping after 25. People: CH, EG, HM, IES, JM, YES. Seeds: 0, 1, 2.

norm/N0cal.title: N0 + 10 s calibration
norm/N0cal.target: Total measured torque, nothing subtracted. The passive table plays no part in training or scoring.

settings: Session 1 → session 2 · 8 angles · one ~90 s trial per angle
4 EMG envelopes (GM, GL, SOL, TA) + ankle angle, 100 Hz
0.2 s = 20 samples → torque at the window’s last sample
Yes: each position’s target ÷ its standard deviation
10 s gain + offset per angle, scored from 30 s
steps: EMG: band-pass 30–300 Hz, rectify, 2 Hz low-pass → envelope (1 kHz), then down-sampled to 100 Hz.
Scale: Each muscle envelope is divided by the largest value it reached anywhere in session 1 (one sample of the 1 kHz envelope). Session 2 is divided by the same four numbers.
Standardise the 5 inputs (mean 0, sd 1) with session 1’s training statistics.
Cut 0.2 s windows sliding by one sample. Each session-1 trial: first 80 % to fit, last 20 % to stop training.
Train the LSTM on the target ÷ each position’s standard deviation, then multiply its predictions back (Nadam, lr 0.003, batch 8, ≤ 200 epochs, early stopping after 25).
Predict every window of session 2, which the model never saw.

Calibrate, without retraining: on the first 10 s of each session-2 trial, fit torque ≈ a × prediction + b (a between 0.5 and 2; offset only if the torque barely moves) and apply it to the whole trial.
Score each position on every 100 Hz sample from 30 s to the end: R² = 1 − Σ(y − ŷ)² / Σ(y − ȳ)², MAE = mean |y − ŷ|. Median over seeds, then median across positions; R² below 0 is shown as 0.

norm/N0cal.purpose: Each muscle is divided by the largest value it reached anywhere in session 1: one single sample of the 1 kHz envelope. Session 2 is divided by the same numbers. This is the control: the same scaling as the baseline. Then a 10 s calibration, no retraining: on the first 10 s of every session-2 trial (torque measured), fit torque ≈ a × prediction + b (a kept between 0.5 and 2; offset only if the person barely pushed) and apply it to the rest of that trial. Scores use only 30 s to the end of each trial, so seconds 0–30 (the calibration block and a gap) are never scored. The trace shows the whole corrected trial.
norm/N0cal.protocol: Train on session 1, test on session 2. Total torque, 0.2 s window (20 samples at 100 Hz) of four muscle envelopes plus angle. Balanced positions (each position’s target ÷ its standard deviation). LSTM 8×2, dropout 0.3, batch 8, at most 200 epochs, early stopping after 25. People: CH, EG, HM, IES, JM, YES. Seeds: 0, 1, 2.
